native_gap: Before OpenClaw runtime admission is active, there is no native runtime primitive that can fail a source-repo phase gate when governance files, registers, review packets, or phase-ledger wiring are incomplete.
requirement_proof: P0/P1 gate movement must fail closed before runtime deployment. A markdown plan or manual reviewer cannot stop an agent from claiming PASS; a deterministic repository validator can return nonzero and block the gate.
alternative_failure_evidence: Manual reviewer output is useful judgment, but the report-card agent found the ledger missing gate_action_report references while reviews existed; without a command returning nonzero, another agent could still claim the gate passed.
Markdown-only checklists cannot fail a command or CI run, and Ryan explicitly rejected rules that only describe concepts without enforcement.
OpenClaw runtime admission is not available until later phases and cannot protect P0/P1 source-repo setup before the runtime foundation exists.
scope: tools/validate_governance.py and governance schema validation only
state_ownership: The validator owns no project state; it reads source files, ledgers, registers, and reports, then exits pass or fail.
failure_mode: If governance evidence is missing, stale, malformed, or inconsistent, the validator exits nonzero and reports the blocking field.
kill_switch: Revert tools/validate_governance.py changes or remove the validator from governance/phase-gates.json enforcement only after an equivalent native runtime gate exists.
rollback: Revert validator changes and the corresponding governance contract fields in phase gates and ledger references.
maintenance_burden: Low; standard library Python, source-repo only, no service, scheduler, network listener, or runtime mutation.
no_second_authority_reason: The validator cannot promote phases, approve tasks, schedule work, or mutate runtime state; it only verifies the existing ledger, reports, and governance contracts.

native_gap: P1 requires proving a clean fork, upstream remote, non-secret environment config, and branch protection evidence before runtime admission exists; no native OpenClaw primitive currently performs this source-control bootstrap check.
requirement_proof: The manual review and P1 checker showed P1 is not pass-qualified without fork/branch-protection proof. A script is required to produce repeatable, non-secret evidence and a read-only checker is required to fail the gate until evidence exists.
alternative_failure_evidence: Manual git remote inspection already went stale in the P1 review: the old review said origin was upstream while current origin was disco32r/openclaw, proving manual observation is not durable enough.
The GitHub CLI is not installed on the VM, and making it a prerequisite would add environment setup friction instead of using standard-library Python already available in the repo runtime.
GitHub UI screenshots alone may help a human, but they do not configure remotes, push a branch, or create machine-checkable p1-branch-protection.json evidence for future agents.
scope: tools/setup_p1_github_environment.py and tools/check_p1_environment.py for P1 source-control bootstrap only
state_ownership: The setup script writes non-secret config and evidence, configures git remotes, and uses GitHub API for fork/protection; the checker only reads repo state and evidence.
failure_mode: If token, fork, push, remotes, or protection evidence are missing, P1 readiness exits nonzero and the phase remains active but blocked.
kill_switch: Remove the scripts from P1 required artifacts and revert P1 config/evidence expectations only after another proven source-control bootstrap path exists.
rollback: Revert remotes to upstream-only if needed, remove non-secret P1 config/evidence files, and revert the scripts and P1 phase-gate references.
tests: python3 -m py_compile tools/setup_p1_github_environment.py tools/check_p1_environment.py; python3 tools/check_p1_environment.py
maintenance_burden: Low to moderate; standard library Python, isolated to P1, external GitHub API only during approved bootstrap.
no_second_authority_reason: The scripts cannot mark P1 PASS or approve protected work; they only create or check evidence consumed by the ledger and validator.

native_gap: Every phase gate action needs a repo-wide compliance report before runtime admission exists; review packets alone judge criteria but do not capture full-repo plan, community-evidence, deny-register, access, changed-file, and Ryan-facing report coverage.
requirement_proof: The manual reviewer found validator enforcement failed because P0/P1 reports were not ledger-linked and stale review text contradicted current remotes. A generated report is required to make every gate action produce consistent, current, repo-wide evidence.
alternative_failure_evidence: Gate review packets can go stale and are phase-criteria focused; the P1 review contained obsolete remote findings after origin and upstream were corrected.
Manual reviewer reports are valuable but not durable governance unless written into the repo and referenced by the ledger; otherwise the output remains chat context.
The validator can enforce report structure, but it cannot itself produce the Ryan-facing report packet with changed files, current mechanical checks, and repo-wide compliance findings.
scope: tools/generate_gate_action_report.py and validator hooks for governance/gate-action-reports
state_ownership: The tool writes evidence reports only; gate authority remains governance/gate-ledger.json plus review packets and validator checks.
failure_mode: If the tool or report is missing, tools/validate_governance.py fails gate validation; if report findings are blocking, PASS gates fail.
kill_switch: Remove the ledger gate_action_report reference or revert this custom-code decision; validator will fail closed until a replacement proof path exists.
rollback: Revert tools/generate_gate_action_report.py, validator report hooks, governance/gate-action-review-contract.md, and gate-action report ledger references.
tests: python3 -m py_compile tools/generate_gate_action_report.py tools/validate_governance.py; python3 tools/generate_gate_action_report.py --gate P1 --action blocked_review --out governance/gate-action-reports/P1-foundation-repo-20260524T1905Z.json; python3 tools/validate_governance.py
maintenance_burden: Low; standard library Python only, source-repo governance scope, no runtime state or scheduler ownership.
no_second_authority_reason: The report generator cannot approve, schedule, route, mutate runtime state, or mark phases done; it only emits evidence consumed by the existing validator and ledger.

native_gap: P4 must cross a protected Docker/runtime boundary before OpenClaw runtime admission exists, and there is no native pre-runtime primitive that can execute the reviewed apply, validation, and rollback commands without manual transcription risk.
requirement_proof: The P4 approval packet is complex, safety-sensitive, and must preserve exact checks for loopback-only ports, pinned image digest, source .env isolation, health/readiness, model status, and rollback. A reviewed one-shot script is required so the approved execution path is durable, repeatable, and syntax-checkable before any protected mutation occurs.
existing_alternatives_checked: manual copy/paste from the approval packet
direct Docker Compose commands in chat
alternative_failure_evidence: Manual packet drafting already found multiple safety corrections after review, including env_file reset, exact rendered Compose JSON validation, and image digest pinning; manual transcription would reintroduce drift risk at the protected boundary.
Chat commands are not durable repo evidence and cannot be validated by the gate process before execution.
Runtime admission primitives are unavailable until P4 has already brought up the private sandbox runtime.
state_ownership: The script owns no authority state; it executes the existing P4 approval packet only when explicitly run with P4_APPROVED=1. Gate authority remains governance/gate-ledger.json, review packets, action reports, and validator output.
failure_mode: If approval is missing, Compose render is invalid, image digest is unpinned, old source .env paths leak, ports are broadly exposed, health/readiness fails, model status fails, or rollback leaves listeners, the script exits nonzero before claiming success.
kill_switch: Stop using the script and revert this file plus the approval-packet references; P4 remains blocked until an equivalent approved execution artifact exists.
rollback: Run P4_APPROVED=1 sh governance/approval-requests/P4-private-sandbox-runtime-20260524T2345Z.sh rollback after approved apply, or revert the script before execution if still source-only.
maintenance_burden: Low; POSIX shell wrapper around reviewed P4 commands, no daemon, scheduler, listener, queue, or independent runtime control plane.
no_second_authority_reason: The script cannot approve protected work, create tasks, schedule agents, route models, mark gates complete, or bypass the validator; it only runs the exact protected commands after explicit approval.
